Subject: Redwood Inference - Multi-region Switchover, RTO/RPO and DR test summary (for Orion Bank RFP)

Executive summary:
Redwood supports predictable, production-grade inference across Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deployments. Our DR strategy emphasizes automated failover where possible, bounded recovery times for committed Dedicated capacity, and well-documented handoffs for Private deployments. Persistent customer data (logs, metrics, audit trails) are stored in encrypted, geo-replicated object storage; ephemeral inference state (KV cache, session context) is treated as cacheable and is rehydratable per request patterns.

RTO / RPO (per offering):
- Hosted API (multi-region routing): RTO: typically 2–10 minutes for routing-level switchover depending on client DNS/edge caching and request routing policies; RPO: near-zero for persisted telemetry and audit logs (replicated within 30s), but ephemeral model inference state (KV cache) is not persisted across region switch — expected cache warm-up up to 15 minutes for first-wave traffic.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): RTO: SLA-backed automated failover target 15 minutes for capacity-failover to warm standby pools within the same cloud provider and 30 minutes for cross-region failover; RPO: persistent request/audit logs replicated cross-region with <60s lag under normal operation; session-level cache is best-effort and may require rewarm (typical rewarm 5–20 minutes depending on model seq-length and workload footprint).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): RTO/RPO are primarily customer-controlled. Redwood provides the private control plane with automated orchestration hooks. Typical engagements include a jointly-run DR runbook; for customers choosing Redwood-managed replication, we recommend a warm-standby configuration with expected switchover of 30–120 minutes depending on network staging.

Automated vs manual switchover steps:
- Automated (Hosted / Dedicated where enabled): health probes -> smart-router switches traffic to healthy region/model variant -> cache-prefix invalidation and pre-warm signals to standby nodes -> announce route via global load balancer or DNS with short TTLs -> post-switchover traffic shaping to prevent thundering herd.
- Manual (Private or high-risk migrations): operator initiates controlled cutover via Console -> promote standby cluster -> verify ingress/egress network ACLs and KMS access -> validate model integrity -> flip routing. Manual procedures are fully documented in attached runbook.

Session & cache behavior (what to expect):
- KV cache: considered ephemeral; in Hosted/Dedicated we use prefix/KV caching to accelerate autoregressive workloads. KV caches are local to serving nodes and are periodically checkpointed to ephemeral warm caches but not to durable storage. On switchover, cache miss rate increases until rewarm completes.
- Rewarm strategies: proactive rewarming (prefetching hot prefixes), retention of warm-standby GPU pools with persisted memory snapshots for Dedicated, and client-side strategies (sticky keys, small context checkpoints) recommended for low-latency session recovery. Typical measured rewarm impact: increased median latency for 5–20 minutes for high context workloads.

Data durability and auditing:
- Persistent artifacts (audit logs, usage records, customer-provided prompt artifacts when retained) are stored encrypted and geo-replicated across regions; retention and encryption controls configurable per customer.

DR test cadence & results:
- Redwood conducts quarterly DR exercises for Hosted and Dedicated stacks. Last full cross-region switchover test: 2026-07-09 — primary -> secondary (same cloud provider, different region) completed in 18 minutes end-to-end with automated routing and cache rewarm strategy; observed customer-visible latency increase for first 12 minutes which returned to baseline by minute 20.
